meta.source: Microsoft Learn study guides and the Microsoft Certifications Poster (Aug 2026)

tracks.tagline: Model, govern and scale analytics on Power BI and Microsoft Fabric.

personas.name: Power BI Developer
personas.summary: Builds semantic models and reports, owns DAX and Power Query, and increasingly works in Git with GitHub Copilot as a pair programmer.

personas.name: Analytics / Fabric Engineer
personas.summary: Takes Power BI to enterprise scale in Fabric: lakehouses, warehouses, pipelines, CI/CD, and agent-assisted engineering workflows.

certifications.title: Azure Data Fundamentals
certifications.whyForUs: Gives you the vocabulary of the wider data platform: relational versus non-relational data, transactional versus analytical workloads, lakehouses, streaming, and where Power BI fits. It's a good warm-up if you have never taken a Microsoft exam.
certifications.audience: Anyone starting to work with data in the cloud.

learningPaths.title: Explore core data concepts
Explore relational data in Azure
Explore non-relational data in Azure
Explore data analytics in Azure

certifications.title: Power BI Data Analyst Associate
certifications.whyForUs: The baseline for the CoE. It validates Power Query, data modeling, DAX, report design, and workspace security. The April 2026 update adds Copilot for report pages, narrative visuals, and model summaries, so AI is now part of the core analyst skill set.
certifications.audience: Power BI analysts and developers who prepare, model, visualize, and secure data.

learningPaths.title: Get started with Microsoft data analytics
Prepare data for analysis with Power BI
Model data with Power BI
Design effective reports in Power BI
Manage and secure Power BI

certifications.title: Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate
certifications.whyForUs: The natural next step after PL-300. It covers enterprise Power BI in Fabric: Direct Lake, lakehouses and warehouses, large semantic models, calculation groups, Git integration with .pbip files, deployment pipelines, and the XMLA endpoint.
certifications.audience: Experienced data professionals who design and deploy enterprise-scale analytics in Fabric.

skills.name: Plan, implement and manage an analytics solution

learningPaths.title: Get started with Microsoft Fabric
Ingest data with Microsoft Fabric
Implement a data warehouse with Microsoft Fabric
Design and manage semantic models in Microsoft Fabric

certifications.title: Fabric Data Engineer Associate
certifications.whyForUs: Takes you out of the report layer and into data architecture and engineering: loading patterns, orchestration, Spark, KQL, streaming, monitoring, and optimization. It helps Power BI developers understand and influence what happens upstream of their models.
certifications.audience: Data professionals who ingest, transform, secure, and operate data engineering solutions in Fabric.

skills.name: Implement and manage an analytics solution
Monitor and optimize an analytics solution

learningPaths.title: Ingest data with Microsoft Fabric
Implement Real-Time Intelligence with Microsoft Fabric
Implement a data warehouse with Microsoft Fabric

certifications.title: Azure AI Fundamentals
certifications.whyForUs: Explains how generative and agentic AI work: models, prompts, responsible AI, and building a simple agent in Microsoft Foundry. It gives you the concepts behind every Copilot feature you use. AI-901 replaced AI-900 in 2026.
certifications.audience: People starting out with AI solutions in Azure. Some Python helps.

skills.name: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry

learningPaths.title: Introduction to AI concepts
Get started with AI apps and agents

certifications.title: GitHub Foundations
certifications.whyForUs: Git and GitHub are now part of Power BI work: .pbip projects, Fabric Git integration, pull requests, and Copilot all depend on them. This is the fastest way to get comfortable with repositories, branches, PRs, and GitHub Projects.
certifications.audience: All GitHub users, developers or not.

learningPaths.title: GitHub Foundations, part 1 of 2
GitHub Foundations, part 2 of 2

certifications.title: GitHub Copilot
certifications.whyForUs: We already use GitHub Copilot, and this certification covers using it well: agent mode, MCP, the Copilot CLI, prompt and context crafting, instruction files, code review, content exclusions, and responsible use. It applies directly to DAX, M, SQL, PySpark, and TMDL work.
certifications.audience: Developers and technical users who already know GitHub fundamentals.

learningPaths.title: GitHub Copilot Fundamentals, part 1 of 2
GitHub Copilot Fundamentals, part 2 of 2
Accelerate app development by using GitHub Copilot

certifications.title: GitHub Certified: Agentic AI Developer
certifications.whyForUs: The developer-level next step after GH-300. It covers running AI agents inside the delivery lifecycle: planning versus execution, tools and MCP servers, memory and state, evaluation, multi-agent orchestration, and guardrails. Choose it if you build or automate pipelines and repositories.
certifications.audience: Engineers who operate, supervise, and govern coding agents in production SDLC workflows.

learningPaths.title: Foundations of agentic AI in GitHub (module)
Designing agent architecture and SDLC integration (module)
Tooling, MCP, and agent execution environments (module)

certifications.title: Enhancing Operational Efficiency with Agentic AI
certifications.whyForUs: An alternative to GH-600 for developers who lean towards analysis and delivery rather than software engineering. It covers designing agentic workflows and automations, custom agents and skills, MCP, and human-in-the-loop review, without deep coding. It is not on the August 2026 poster yet and is still in beta.
certifications.audience: Business-leaning roles (BA, PM, TPM) who use GitHub and Copilot to automate work.

learningPaths.title: GitHub Copilot documentation (no Learn path yet)

certifications.title: AI Business Professional
certifications.whyForUs: Focused on Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Cowork, and prebuilt agents for everyday business work, with no code. It's useful for working with report consumers, but it adds little to development skills. Updated on 20 Oct 2026.
certifications.audience: Business professionals who use M365 Copilot and agents in daily work.

skills.name: Prompts and chats in M365 Copilot

certifications.title: SQL AI Developer Associate
certifications.whyForUs: Combines the two tracks: advanced T-SQL, SQL Database Projects with CI/CD in GitHub, GitHub Copilot and MCP for SQL, embeddings, vector and hybrid search, and RAG, on SQL Server, Azure SQL, and SQL databases in Fabric.
certifications.audience: Database developers who build AI-enabled SQL solutions.

skills.name: Secure, optimize and deploy database solutions
Implement AI capabilities in database solutions

certifications.title: Azure Databricks Data Engineer Associate
certifications.whyForUs: Relevant if your data platform is Databricks rather than, or alongside, Fabric. It covers Unity Catalog governance, Lakeflow pipelines and jobs, and Databricks Asset Bundles.
certifications.audience: Data engineers who build and operate pipelines in Azure Databricks.

skills.name: Set up and configure Azure Databricks
Deploy and maintain pipelines and workloads

learningPaths.title: Course DP-750T00: Implement data engineering solutions using Azure Databricks

certifications.title: Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate
certifications.whyForUs: For people who want to move from using AI to building it: RAG, agents, and multi-agent solutions in Microsoft Foundry with Python. It's a career pivot towards AI engineering rather than a Power BI step.
certifications.audience: Azure AI engineers who build and deploy agents and AI apps on Foundry.

skills.name: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
